source_collection: Kendra AI BIR public evaluation sample pack
source_approval_scope: Local Kendra AI development and evaluation only

cases.question: When was Revenue Regulations No. 2-2024 issued?
expected_answer_facts: Revenue Regulations No. 2-2024 was issued on February 28, 2024.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Giving another issuance date, omitting the source page, or presenting the date as current tax advice.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The requested date is the issuance date printed in this one-page source, not its download or approval date.

cases.question: Under RR No. 3-2024, what single term replaces references to gross selling price, gross value in money, and gross receipts?
expected_answer_facts: All three references are replaced by the term gross sales.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Using gross receipts as the replacement term or failing to cite page 1.
cases.ambiguity_notes: Capitalization is not material; the consolidation of all three former terms is material.

cases.question: What filing method does RR No. 4-2024 prescribe, and what exception permits manual filing?
expected_answer_facts: Tax returns are to be filed electronically on any available electronic platform.
Manual filing may be allowed when the electronic platforms are unavailable.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Saying manual filing is generally optional or omitting the electronic-platform unavailability condition.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The question concerns filing, not the separate electronic or manual payment alternatives on the same page.

cases.question: Under RR No. 4-2024, when may two self-employed spouses file separate income tax returns instead of one joint return?
expected_answer_facts: Separate filing is allowed when filing one return is impracticable.
The document gives spouses whose businesses are registered under two different RDOs as an example.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Treating separate filing as the default or inventing additional exceptions.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The different-RDO scenario is an example of impracticability, not an exhaustive definition in this source.

cases.question: Does RR No. 11-2024 require a business taxpayer to replace an existing Certificate of Registration merely because it displays the Registration Fee?
expected_answer_facts: No replacement is required merely because the Registration Fee is displayed.
The existing Certificate of Registration remains valid.
Updating is necessary only when registration information other than the Registration Fee changes.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Requiring automatic replacement or omitting the exception for changes to other registration information.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The answer is limited to the transitory rule shown in the supplied document.

cases.question: What deadline and filing quantity did RR No. 11-2024 set for the inventory of unused manual and loose-leaf receipts to be converted to invoices?
expected_answer_facts: The inventory was due on or before July 31, 2024.
It was to be submitted in duplicate copies.
It was to identify the number of booklets and corresponding serial numbers.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Giving December 31, 2024 as the inventory deadline or omitting the duplicate-copy requirement.
cases.ambiguity_notes: December 31 applies to machine or system reconfiguration, not this manual and loose-leaf inventory.

cases.question: By when did RR No. 11-2024 require CAS or CBA with Accounting Records adjustments, and what was the maximum extension?
expected_answer_facts: Adjustments were to be undertaken on or before December 31, 2024.
An approved extension could not be longer than six months from December 31, 2024.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Calling the extension automatic or longer than six months.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The approval authority is relevant context but not required unless the response states that an extension is automatic.

cases.question: What two dates does RMC No. 3-2024 give for its issuance and for the signing of RA No. 11976 and its Veto Message?
expected_answer_facts: RMC No. 3-2024 was issued on January 10, 2024.
RA No. 11976 and the Veto Message were signed on January 5, 2024.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Conflating the two dates or attributing the circular's issue date to the Act.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The source says both the Act and Veto Message were signed on January 5, 2024.

cases.question: Within how many days from the EOPT Act's effectivity were implementing rules and regulations to be promulgated, according to RMC No. 3-2024?
expected_answer_facts: The period was ninety calendar days from the effectivity of the Act.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Changing calendar days to working days or calculating a calendar date not stated on the cited page.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The source gives a relative period; this case does not ask the evaluator to infer an absolute deadline.

cases.question: How long does Annex A1 give an applicant to submit identified lacking requirements, and when may a pending incomplete application be disposed?
expected_answer_facts: The applicant commits to submit identified lacking requirements within five working days.
The BIR may dispose of a pending application with incomplete requirements after thirty calendar days from receipt of the application.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Conflating five working days with thirty calendar days or omitting the starting event for the thirty-day period.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The two periods govern different statements on the form.

cases.question: What corporate registration document does Annex A2.1 accept for a foreign corporation?
expected_answer_facts: A photocopy of the License to Do Business in the Philippines is accepted for a foreign corporation.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Substituting a domestic SEC Certificate of Incorporation without noting the foreign-corporation alternative.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The license is one branch of an either-or list in item 2.

cases.question: For procurement project 2024-001, what total ABC and total contract cost are reported?
expected_answer_facts: The total ABC is PhP 2,730,755.00.
The total contract cost is PhP 2,622,648.24.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Swapping ABC and contract cost, dropping cents, or using another project's row.
cases.ambiguity_notes: Use the Total columns, not the MOOE or CO subcolumns; for this row the MOOE values happen to match the totals.

cases.question: What total allotted budget and total contract cost are shown for ongoing procurement activities?
expected_answer_facts: The total allotted budget for ongoing procurement activities is PhP 175,284,574.00.
The total contract cost shown for ongoing procurement activities is PhP 169,021,829.87.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Using the completed-procurement totals from page 13 or reporting an MOOE or CO subtotal as the overall total.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The report labels the second three-number group under Contract Cost even though the total-line label begins with Total Allotted Budget.

cases.question: According to RMC No. 77-2024, when must a VAT-registered person issue a VAT invoice?
expected_answer_facts: A VAT-registered person must issue a duly registered VAT invoice for every sale, barter, exchange, or lease of goods or properties and every sale, barter, or exchange of services.
The requirement applies regardless of the amount of the transaction.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Applying the PhP 500 threshold to VAT-registered sellers or failing to cite the scanned page.
cases.ambiguity_notes: This is Q1/A1; the nearby PhP 500 rule concerns non-VAT sellers.

cases.question: According to RMC No. 77-2024 Q2, when must a non-VAT seller issue an invoice for a transaction?
expected_answer_facts: A non-VAT seller must issue an invoice when a single sale is PhP 500.00 or more.
An invoice must also be issued when the buyer requests one, regardless of amount.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Saying the threshold applies to VAT sellers or omitting the buyer-request exception.
cases.ambiguity_notes: Q3 on page 2 uses 'more than PhP 500.00' and adds an end-of-day aggregation rule. This case is deliberately scoped to Q2 on page 1, which says PhP 500.00 or more.

cases.question: How and from what starting point is the PhP 500 invoice threshold to be adjusted under RMC No. 77-2024?
expected_answer_facts: The threshold is to be adjusted to present value every three years.
The cycle begins January 22, 2024, the effectivity date of the EOPT Act.
The adjustment uses the Consumer Price Index published by the Philippine Statistics Authority.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Inventing an adjusted peso amount or a different starting date.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The source specifies the method and cycle but not a future adjusted threshold.

cases.question: Does RMC No. 77-2024 require the buyer's or seller's business style to appear on an invoice?
expected_answer_facts: No, business style is not required on the invoice.
A seller may indicate its business name for trade name, store name identification, or branding.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Turning the optional business-name statement into a mandatory field.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The answer distinguishes business style from an optionally shown business name.

cases.question: Is prior RDO, LT Office, or LT Division approval required to stamp 'Invoice' on remaining unused Official Receipts?
expected_answer_facts: No prior approval is required for the stamping.
The reporting requirement still applies.
Newly printed invoices with an Authority to Print should be obtained before the converted receipts are fully consumed.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Saying no approval means no reporting or replacement-printing obligations.
cases.ambiguity_notes: This is Q20/A20 and should not be confused with approvals for system-extension requests on page 9.

cases.question: What deadline and maximum extension does RMC No. 77-2024 state for enhancing a CAS or CBA with Accounting Records?
expected_answer_facts: The enhancement was to be completed on or before December 31, 2024.
An approved extension could not exceed six months from December 31, 2024.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Treating the extension as automatic or open-ended.
cases.ambiguity_notes: Q24 on the same page gives the request procedure and decision timelines; this case asks only deadline and maximum duration.

cases.question: When did the invoicing provisions of RR No. 7-2024 become effective according to RMC No. 77-2024?
expected_answer_facts: The invoicing provisions became effective on April 27, 2024.
That was fifteen days from publication on the BIR official website on April 12, 2024.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Using April 12 as the effectivity date or omitting the fifteen-day relationship when explaining the date.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The circular itself states it takes effect immediately upon website posting on page 12; this question asks about RR No. 7-2024's invoicing provisions.

cases.question: List the three publication channels identified in RR No. 2-2024 for BIR issuances.
expected_answer_facts: BIR official website
Official Gazette
Newspaper of general circulation
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Adding social media or another channel not listed on the page, or omitting one of the three channels.
cases.ambiguity_notes: Electronic or otherwise describes publishing mode; it is not a fourth named channel.

cases.question: Which eleven categories of BIR issuances or information materials are listed as subject to RR No. 2-2024?
expected_answer_facts: Revenue Regulations
Revenue Memorandum Circulars
Revenue Memorandum Orders
Other revenue issuances
Classification of taxpayers, including Top Withholding Agents
Cannot be located taxpayers
Revised Schedules of Zonal Values
List of seized, foreclosed and acquired properties for sale
Notice of sale of seized, foreclosed and acquired properties
Information materials such as press releases, announcements or advisories, and flyers
Other similar documents or materials that require publication
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Returning only examples, merging distinct list and notice-of-sale categories, or inventing categories.
cases.ambiguity_notes: Equivalent punctuation and expansion of CBL as cannot be located are acceptable.

cases.question: Which final three NIRC sections on RMC No. 3-2024's amended-section list appear on page 2, and which provision does the circular say was repealed?
expected_answer_facts: Section 245, Specific Provisions to be Contained in Rules and Regulations
Section 248, Civil Penalties
Section 269, Violations Committed by Government Enforcement Officers
Section 34(K) was repealed, with the succeeding paragraph renumbered accordingly
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Omitting the repeal, citing page 1 alone, or treating Section 34(K) as part of the amended list.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The amended-section list begins on page 1 and continues with these final entries on page 2.

cases.question: List the six top-level groups of registration and invoicing requirements summarized in RR No. 7-2024.
expected_answer_facts: Invoicing and Accounting Requirements for VAT-Registered Persons
Preservation of Books of Accounts and Other Accounting Records
Registration Requirements
Issuance of Invoices
Printing of Invoices
Transitory Provisions
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Returning only subitems or omitting one of groups A through F.
cases.ambiguity_notes: Section numbers may be included but are not required if all six group names are correct.

cases.question: List the six base documentary requirements shown in Annex A1 for self-employed persons, professionals, and mixed-income earners.
expected_answer_facts: BIR Form No. 1901
Government-issued identification showing name, address, and birthdate
Mayor's Business Permit or a duly received application if still in process, and/or a Professional or Occupational Tax Receipt, or a DTI Certificate
Proof of payment of Registration Fee when applicable
BIR Form No. 1906 with selection of an Accredited Printer
Final and clear sample of principal receipts or invoices
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Mixing the separate additional-if-applicable list into the six base items or omitting alternatives in item 3.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The page repeats the checklist as BIR and taxpayer copies; duplicated layout does not double the requirements.

cases.question: Create a three-row table of the special registration documents required by Annex A2.2 for GAIs or LGUs, foreign embassies, and international organizations.
expected_answer_facts: GAIs and LGUs: BIR Form No. 1903 and a photocopy of the unit or agency charter
Foreign embassies: BIR Form No. 1903 and endorsement from the Department of Foreign Affairs
International organizations: BIR Form No. 1903 and a host agreement or other international agreement duly certified by the Department of Foreign Affairs
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Dropping BIR Form No. 1903 from a row or substituting cooperative or homeowners-association documents.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The Special Power of Attorney item is conditional and common context, not one of the entity-specific core rows requested.

cases.question: Provide a table showing project number, PMO or end-user, early-procurement status, total ABC, and total contract cost for projects 2024-001, 2024-002, and 2024-005.
expected_answer_facts: 2024-001: AHRMD; Yes; PhP 2,730,755.00 ABC; PhP 2,622,648.24 contract cost
2024-002: RID; Yes; PhP 4,166,000.00 ABC; PhP 4,017,075.12 contract cost
2024-005: AHRMD; No; PhP 1,278,711.42 ABC; PhP 1,275,339.12 contract cost
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Misaligning values across landscape-table rows or columns, or rounding away centavos.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The requested financial values are the Total columns, not MOOE or CO subcolumns.

cases.question: Tabulate the total, MOOE, and CO values for completed procurement's allotted budget and contract price, and give the reported savings.
expected_answer_facts: Allotted budget: total PhP 25,559,809.52; MOOE PhP 20,591,481.52; CO PhP 4,968,328.00
Contract price: total PhP 23,262,041.75; MOOE PhP 18,341,301.75; CO PhP 4,920,740.00
Reported total savings: PhP 2,297,767.77
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Using ongoing-procurement totals from page 15, swapping MOOE and CO, or recomputing a different value without reporting the source's stated savings.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The savings row reports only an overall total, not separate MOOE and CO savings.

cases.question: List the eight invoice labels illustrated in RMC No. 77-2024 Q13 and state the transaction purpose given for each.
expected_answer_facts: Invoice: both sales of goods or services rendered
Sales Invoice: general-purpose invoice for any sales transaction
Cash Invoice: cash sales or sales where immediate payment is received
Charge or Credit Invoice: credit sales where payment is expected later
Service Invoice: transactions where a service is provided
Billing Invoice: billing charges, similar to a charge invoice and statements of account or billing statements
Commercial Invoice: export transactions
Miscellaneous Invoice: other income received by the seller
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Omitting a label, assigning a purpose to the wrong label, or treating examples as exclusive legal definitions beyond the page.
cases.ambiguity_notes: Charge Invoice and Credit Invoice are presented as one combined purpose in the source list.

cases.question: Which five missing invoice fields does RMC No. 77-2024 Q29 identify as exceptions that can prevent a VAT amount from being used as input tax credit?
expected_answer_facts: Amount of sales
VAT amount
Registered name and TIN shown on the BIR Certificate of Registration of both purchaser or buyer and issuer or seller
Description of goods or nature of services
Date of transaction
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Citing Q28 on page 10 alone or omitting that the registered name and TIN apply to both sides of the transaction.
cases.ambiguity_notes: Q28 on page 10 contains a closely related five-field list; this case specifically asks for Q29, which is on page 11.

cases.question: How do RR No. 3-2024 and RMC No. 77-2024 together distinguish invoice terminology and the invoicing threshold for VAT and non-VAT sellers?
expected_answer_facts: RR No. 3-2024 says Invoice replaces Sales or Commercial Invoices and Official Receipts as terminology.
RMC No. 77-2024 requires a VAT invoice for every VAT sale regardless of amount.
RMC No. 77-2024 applies the PhP 500 threshold to non-VAT sellers, with an invoice also required on buyer request regardless of amount.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Applying the PhP 500 threshold to VAT sellers or attributing the threshold rule to RR No. 3-2024.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The circular clarifies implementation; the comparison does not establish currentness beyond the supplied 2024 sources.

cases.question: What relationship between RR No. 7-2024 and RR No. 11-2024 is shown by the supplied summaries?
expected_answer_facts: RR No. 7-2024 summarizes registration procedures and invoicing requirements, including transitory provisions.
RR No. 11-2024 amends RR No. 7-2024's transitory provisions concerning deadlines for compliance with invoicing requirements.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Claiming RR No. 11-2024 repeals all of RR No. 7-2024 or inventing a supersession relationship.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The supplied material establishes an amendment to transitory provisions, not comprehensive current legal status.

cases.question: Compare the manual or loose-leaf inventory-report deadline in RR No. 11-2024 with the Annex C clarification in RMC No. 77-2024.
expected_answer_facts: RR No. 11-2024 requires the inventory by July 31, 2024, in duplicate, with booklet counts and serial numbers.
RMC No. 77-2024 identifies Annex C as the inventory-report format for manual or loose-leaf receipts and gives July 31, 2024 as the deadline.

RMC No. 77-2024 says taxpayers who already submitted an inventory report using Annex D of RMO No. 12-2013 or a Letter Notice before the circular's website publication need not resubmit in the new Annex C or D format.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Using the Annex D machine-renaming deadline as the Annex C inventory deadline or omitting the no-resubmission exception.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The same label Annex D appears in an older RMO and in this circular; the answer must preserve the source context.

cases.question: Do RR No. 11-2024 and RMC No. 77-2024 state the same CAS or CBA enhancement deadline and extension limit?
expected_answer_facts: Yes; both state an adjustment or enhancement deadline on or before December 31, 2024.
Both limit an approved extension to no more than six months from December 31, 2024.
Both identify approval by the concerned Regional Director or Assistant Commissioner of the Large Taxpayers Service.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Calling the extension automatic or saying the documents give different deadlines.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The circular provides additional request-procedure detail, but the common deadline and limit are the comparison target.

cases.question: Compare the penalty stated in RR No. 11-2024 with RMC No. 77-2024 for non-issuance of a required invoice after the applicable transition period.
expected_answer_facts: Both state a fine of not less than PhP 1,000.00 and not more than PhP 50,000.00.
Both state imprisonment of not less than two years and not more than four years.
Both cite Section 264(a) of the Tax Code.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Changing the minimum or maximum amounts or imprisonment terms, or citing only one document for a comparison answer.
cases.ambiguity_notes: RMC No. 77-2024 has related penalty discussion in Q27; Q26 on page 10 most directly mirrors RR No. 11-2024's transition language.

cases.question: Which NIRC sections listed as amended in RMC No. 3-2024 are also named as the implementation scope of RR No. 7-2024?
expected_answer_facts: Section 113
Section 235
Section 236
Section 237
Section 238
Section 242
Section 243
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Including sections that appear in only one of the two lists or omitting shared sections.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The comparison is an exact set intersection of the two supplied page lists.

cases.question: Compare the issue date and principal subject of RR No. 3-2024 and RR No. 4-2024.
expected_answer_facts: Both were issued on April 11, 2024.
RR No. 3-2024 addresses EOPT changes to VAT and percentage tax, including terminology and related amendments.
RR No. 4-2024 addresses filing tax returns, payment of taxes, and matters affecting declaration of taxable income.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Conflating their subjects or assigning a different issue date to either regulation.
cases.ambiguity_notes: This compares the summaries' principal subjects, not every Tax Code section they cover.

cases.question: What common conditions do RR No. 11-2024 and RMC No. 77-2024 place on converting an unused Official Receipt into an invoice?
expected_answer_facts: The old Official Receipt wording is struck through and an invoice label is stamped on the face.
The converted document must contain required invoice information, including quantity, unit cost, and description of goods or nature of service.
Missing required information may be stamped on the document.
The converted receipts may be used until fully consumed.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Saying unchanged Official Receipts automatically become invoices or omitting required invoice information.
cases.ambiguity_notes: RMC Q10 on page 3 contains the requested common conditions; Q11 on page 4 provides a sample-specific reiteration and is not required for this answer.

cases.question: How does RR No. 7-2024's registration scope relate to the concrete Annex A1 checklist for a self-employed applicant?
expected_answer_facts: RR No. 7-2024 identifies registration requirements under Section 236, including manner and time, place, business registration, business name, registration date, certificates, posting, tax types, cancellation, transfer, and unlawful pursuit of business.

Annex A1 supplies concrete applicant documents, including BIR Form No. 1901, government identification, permit or registration alternatives, proof of registration-fee payment when applicable, BIR Form No. 1906, and a sample receipt or invoice.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Claiming the RR summary itself lists the Annex A1 applicant documents or treating the checklist as proof of current legal status.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The two sources operate at different levels: a regulatory topic summary and a form-layout checklist.

cases.question: What do RMC No. 3-2024 and RR No. 4-2024 say about withholding-tax provisions that were vetoed or repealed?
expected_answer_facts: RMC No. 3-2024 says the provision granting micro-enterprises exemption from the obligation to withhold taxes was vetoed by the President.
RR No. 4-2024 says Section 2.58.5 of RR No. 2-98 on additional deductibility requirements was repealed upon EOPT effectivity.
RR No. 4-2024 expressly says the obligation to withhold tax on certain income payments and remit it remains.
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Concluding that all withholding obligations were eliminated or merging the veto and repeal into one event.
cases.ambiguity_notes: These are separate provisions and legal actions; the answer must preserve that distinction.

cases.question: What is the current VAT rate in the Philippines for tax year 2025?
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Supplying a rate from general knowledge, memory, or an uncited source instead of rejecting the question as unsupported by this corpus.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The source discusses VAT terminology and amendments but does not state the requested 2025 rate.

cases.question: Is RR No. 7-2024 still the controlling invoicing regulation as of August 15, 2026?
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Claiming currentness or controlling status from the absence of a later source in this bounded 2024 sample.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The corpus shows a 2024 amendment and clarification but contains no authoritative status register through 2026.

cases.question: What exact peso amount did the PhP 500 invoice threshold become after its first CPI adjustment?
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Calculating, guessing, or inventing an adjusted amount from the stated adjustment method.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The sources state a three-year CPI adjustment rule but no later CPI input or adjusted threshold.

cases.question: Who is the Commissioner of Internal Revenue as of August 15, 2026?
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Using the 2024 signatory on page 12 as proof of officeholder status in 2026.
cases.ambiguity_notes: A historical signature does not establish a later current officeholder.

cases.question: Which supplier or contractor was awarded procurement project 2024-001?
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Mistaking the PMO or end-user, source of funds, or project description for the awarded supplier.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The supplied monitoring-report columns do not identify a supplier or contractor for the row.

cases.question: How many bids were received for procurement project 2024-001?
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Inferring a bid count from the Sub/Open of Bids date or from the project's competitive-bidding mode.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The report records dates and mode but not a count of bids received.

cases.question: What exact email address should a taxpayer use to submit Annex C or Annex D reports?
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Inventing an email address or converting a named office or portal into an address.
cases.ambiguity_notes: Page 8 mentions submission through the TRRA portal via email of the Compliance Section but supplies no exact email address.

cases.question: What monetary fine applies when a registration applicant fails to submit incomplete Annex A1 requirements?
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Importing the invoice non-issuance penalty from another document or treating disposal after thirty days as a monetary fine.
cases.ambiguity_notes: Annex A1 states a five-working-day commitment and possible disposal after thirty calendar days, but no monetary fine.

cases.question: Which later issuance superseded RR No. 11-2024?
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Assuming a superseding issuance exists or naming one from memory without corpus evidence.
cases.ambiguity_notes: The supplied pack contains no later status or supersession evidence for RR No. 11-2024.

cases.question: What OCR character-accuracy percentage was achieved on RMC No. 77-2024?
cases.unacceptable_answer_behavior: Inventing an OCR metric, treating visual readability as a measured percentage, or citing a source page as if it reports OCR performance.
cases.ambiguity_notes: OCR accuracy is an evaluation or processing metric, not a fact contained in the source PDF.
